claim: The segregation of the trophectoderm (TE) from the inner cell mass (ICM) in the mouse blastocyst is determined by position-dependent Hippo signaling.
source: The segregation of the trophectoderm (TE) from the inner cell mass (ICM) in the mouse blastocyst is determined by position-dependent Hippo signaling.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that references established knowledge in the field.

claim: The TE transcriptional profile stabilizes earlier than the ICM and prior to blastocyst formation.
source: Single-cell RNA sequencing during lineage segregation revealed that the TE transcriptional profile stabilizes earlier than the ICM and prior to blastocyst formation.
evidence: This claim is supported by single-cell RNA sequencing data presented in the manuscript.

claim: TE specification and commitment coincide and occur at the time of transcriptional stabilization.
source: We find that TE specification and commitment coincide and occur at the time of transcriptional stabilization, whereas ICM cells still retain the ability to regenerate TE up to the early blastocyst stage.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from morula aggregation and embryo reconstruction assays.

claim: ICM cells retain the ability to regenerate TE up to the early blastocyst stage.
source: We find that TE specification and commitment coincide and occur at the time of transcriptional stabilization, whereas ICM cells still retain the ability to regenerate TE up to the early blastocyst stage.
evidence: This is supported by embryo reconstruction experiments showing ICM cells can form TE until the 64 cell stage.

claim: Plasticity of both lineages is coincident with their window of sensitivity to Hippo signaling.
source: Plasticity of both lineages is coincident with their window of sensitivity to Hippo signaling.
evidence: This is supported by ROCKi treatment and DN Lats2 induction experiments.

claim: The TE is an extraembryonic tissue, giving rise to the trophoblast lineages of the placenta.
source: The TE is an extraembryonic tissue, giving rise to the trophoblast lineages of the placenta.
evidence: This is established knowledge about TE lineage fate.

claim: The ICM will form two additional lineages before implantation - the pluripotent epiblast (EPI), giving rise to all germ layers of the embryo, and the primitive endoderm (PE), largely forming the endoderm layers of the yolk sacs.
source: The ICM will form two additional lineages before implantation - the pluripotent epiblast (EPI), giving rise to all germ layers of the embryo, and the primitive endoderm (PE), largely forming the endoderm layers of the yolk sacs (Cockburn and Rossant, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: At the blastocyst stage, the TE forms a monolayer tight junction-coupled epithelium enclosing the blastocoelic cavity, at one end of which lies the ICM.
source: At the blastocyst stage, the TE forms a monolayer tight junction-coupled epithelium enclosing the blastocoelic cavity, at one end of which lies the ICM.
evidence: This is established knowledge about blastocyst structure.

claim: Inside and outside cell populations first form following the 8 to 16 cell divisions.
source: Inside and outside cell populations first form following the 8 to 16 cell divisions (Anani et al., 2014; Dietrich and Hiiragi, 2007; Watanabe et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: During the 16 cell stage and during the 16 to 32 cell divisions, division-independent and dependent cell internalization leads to dynamic morphological rearrangements.
source: During the 16 cell stage and during the 16 to 32 cell divisions, division-independent and dependent cell internalization leads to dynamic morphological rearrangements (Anani et al., 2014; Maître et al., 2016; Morris et al., 2010; Samarage et al., 2015; Watanabe et al., 2014; Yamanaka et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: From the 32 cell stage onwards, apart from the relatively rare event of division-independent cell internalization, inside and outside positioning is generally a good indicator of ICM and TE lineage fates, respectively.
source: From the 32 cell stage onwards, apart from the relatively rare event of division-independent cell internalization, inside and outside positioning is generally a good indicator of ICM and TE lineage fates, respectively (McDole et al., 2011; McDole and Zheng, 2012; Pedersen et al., 1986; Watanabe et al., 2014; Toyooka et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: During the 8 to 16 cell divisions, cells inherit varying amounts of apically localized proteins from the apical domain – the polarized outside surface forming at the 8 cell stage.
source: During the 8 to 16 cell divisions, cells inherit varying amounts of apically localized proteins from the apical domain – the polarized outside surface forming at the 8 cell stage (Anani et al., 2014; Johnson and Ziomek, 1981; Korotkevich et al., 2017; Watanabe et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Inside cells are apolar, while outside cells can either be apolar or polar.
source: Inside cells are apolar, while outside cells can either be apolar or polar.
evidence: This is established knowledge about cell polarity in early embryos.

claim: Outside apolar cells were identified as the cells that internalize during the 16 cell stage in a division-independent manner.
source: Interestingly, outside apolar cells were identified as the cells that internalize during the 16 cell stage in a division-independent manner (Anani et al., 2014; Maître et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Individual blastomeres show variation in gene expression and epigenetic marks prior to the 8 cell stage, and these differences may bias their future fate.
source: Although there is some evidence that individual blastomeres show variation in gene expression and epigenetic marks prior to the 8 cell stage, and that these differences may bias their future fate (Biase et al., 2014; Burton et al., 2013; Goolam et al., 2016; Plachta et al., 2011; Torres-Padilla et al., 2007; White et al., 2016), it is also clear that polarity differences are key to final assignment of cell fate.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Polarity differences are key to final assignment of cell fate.
source: Although there is some evidence that individual blastomeres show variation in gene expression and epigenetic marks prior to the 8 cell stage, and that these differences may bias their future fate (Biase et al., 2014; Burton et al., 2013; Goolam et al., 2016; Plachta et al., 2011; Torres-Padilla et al., 2007; White et al., 2016), it is also clear that polarity differences are key to final assignment of cell fate.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge and the context of the manuscript.

claim: Polarity differences result in differential activation of the Hippo signaling pathway: active Hippo signaling in apolar cells sequesters the transcriptional co-activator Yap into the cytoplasm, while inactive Hippo in polar cells allows nuclear accumulation of Yap, and its interaction with the transcription factor Tead4.
source: Polarity differences result in differential activation of the Hippo signaling pathway: active Hippo signaling in apolar cells sequesters the transcriptional co-activator Yap into the cytoplasm, while inactive Hippo in polar cells allows nuclear accumulation of Yap, and its interaction with the transcription factor Tead4 (Hirate et al., 2013; Nishioka et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Nuclear Yap/Tead4 complexes are required for TE formation and are upstream regulators of Cdx2, a key TE-specific transcription factor.
source: Nuclear Yap/Tead4 complexes are required for TE formation and are upstream regulators of Cdx2, a key TE-specific transcription factor (Kaneko and DePamphilis, 2013; Nishioka et al., 2009, 2008; Rayon et al., 2014; Yagi et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Activation of Cdx2 expression in TE progenitors leads to downregulation of the pluripotent factors, Oct4 and Nanog.
source: Activation of Cdx2 expression in TE progenitors leads to downregulation of the pluripotent factors, Oct4 and Nanog (Chen et al., 2009; Niwa et al., 2005; Strumpf et al., 2005), while in ICM progenitors Hippo signaling leads to upregulation of Sox2, a co-factor with Oct4 in pluripotency (Wicklow et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In ICM progenitors Hippo signaling leads to upregulation of Sox2, a co-factor with Oct4 in pluripotency.
source: Activation of Cdx2 expression in TE progenitors leads to downregulation of the pluripotent factors, Oct4 and Nanog (Chen et al., 2009; Niwa et al., 2005; Strumpf et al., 2005), while in ICM progenitors Hippo signaling leads to upregulation of Sox2, a co-factor with Oct4 in pluripotency (Wicklow et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous study.

claim: Differential Hippo activity is a key driver of ICM-TE lineage segregation.
source: Thus differential Hippo activity is a key driver of ICM-TE lineage segregation.
evidence: This is inferred from the preceding discussion of Hippo signaling's role.

claim: The exact time when differential Hippo signaling is instructive to establish cell fate is not known.
source: However, the exact time when differential Hippo signaling is instructive to establish cell fate is not known.
evidence: This identifies a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: Inner cells were reported to have lost TE-forming potential by the 32 cell stage.
source: For example, inner cells were reported to have lost TE-forming potential by the 32 cell stage (Tarkowski et al., 2010), the early-mid blastocyst (~64 cell) stage (Handyside, 1978; Rossant and Lis, 1979; Stephenson et al., 2010; Suwińska et al., 2008) or the late blastocyst stage (Grabarek et al., 2012; Hogan and Tilly, 1978; Spindle, 1978).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous study.

claim: Inner cells were reported to have lost TE-forming potential by the early-mid blastocyst (~64 cell) stage.
source: For example, inner cells were reported to have lost TE-forming potential by the 32 cell stage (Tarkowski et al., 2010), the early-mid blastocyst (~64 cell) stage (Handyside, 1978; Rossant and Lis, 1979; Stephenson et al., 2010; Suwińska et al., 2008) or the late blastocyst stage (Grabarek et al., 2012; Hogan and Tilly, 1978; Spindle, 1978).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Inner cells were reported to have lost TE-forming potential by the late blastocyst stage.
source: For example, inner cells were reported to have lost TE-forming potential by the 32 cell stage (Tarkowski et al., 2010), the early-mid blastocyst (~64 cell) stage (Handyside, 1978; Rossant and Lis, 1979; Stephenson et al., 2010; Suwińska et al., 2008) or the late blastocyst stage (Grabarek et al., 2012; Hogan and Tilly, 1978; Spindle, 1978).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Outside cells were found to retain some plasticity up to the 32 cell stage.
source: Outside cells were found to retain some plasticity up to the 32 cell stage (Rossant and Vijh, 1980; Tarkowski et al., 2010) but lost ICM potential when cavitation occurred during 32 cell stage (Suwińska et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Outside cells lost ICM potential when cavitation occurred during 32 cell stage.
source: Outside cells were found to retain some plasticity up to the 32 cell stage (Rossant and Vijh, 1980; Tarkowski et al., 2010) but lost ICM potential when cavitation occurred during 32 cell stage (Suwińska et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous study.

claim: eGFP expression faithfully mimics endogenous Cdx2 expression dynamics.
source: Using a Cdx2-eGFP fusion knock-in mouse line (McDole and Zheng, 2012) we confirmed that eGFP expression faithfully mimics endogenous Cdx2 expression dynamics (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Cdx2-eGFP expression was first clearly detectable in early 16 cell embryos and gradually became restricted to the outer layer of the TE.
source: Expression was first clearly detectable in early 16 cell embryos and gradually became restricted to the outer layer of the TE.
evidence: This is based on observations from the Cdx2-eGFP mouse line.

claim: eGFP and endogenous Cdx2 fluorescent signals in Cdx2-eGFP heterozygous embryos showed a significant correlation from the 16 cell stage onwards.
source: We found that eGFP and endogenous Cdx2 fluorescent signals in Cdx2-eGFP heterozygous embryos showed a significant correlation from the 16 cell stage onwards.
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: From the early 16 cell stage onward, inside cells expressed on average significantly lower eGFP levels than outside cells.
source: We found that even from the early 16 cell stage onward, inside cells expressed on average significantly lower eGFP levels than outside cells.
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Initially some inside and outside cells had overlapping eGFP levels, which gradually segregated by the late 32 cell stage.
source: However, initially some inside and outside cells had overlapping eGFP levels, which gradually segregated by the late 32 cell stage.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Cdx2 expression is initiated in a heterogeneous, Tead4-independent manner at the morula stage, whilst later expression requires nuclear Yap/Tead4 activity in TE progenitor cells.
source: Cdx2 expression is initiated in a heterogeneous, Tead4-independent manner at the morula stage, whilst later expression requires nuclear Yap/Tead4 activity in TE progenitor cells (Nishioka et al., 2009, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Yap localization is regulated by Hippo signaling in the preimplantation embryo.
source: Yap localization is in turn regulated by Hippo signaling in the preimplantation embryo (Cockburn et al., 2013; Nishioka et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: As soon as shuttling of nuclear Yap to the cytoplasm was initiated at the early 16 cell stage, Cdx2-eGFP levels started to show a positive correlation with n/c Yap ratios.
source: We found that as soon as shuttling of nuclear Yap to the cytoplasm was initiated at the early 16 cell stage, Cdx2-eGFP levels started to show a positive correlation with n/c Yap ratios.
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The positive correlation between Cdx2-eGFP levels and n/c Yap ratios progressively increased up to the early 32 cell stage.
source: This positive correlation progressively increased up to the early 32 cell stage.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Emerging Hippo signaling differences, starting at the early 16 cell stage, rapidly seize control of Cdx2 expression and up-regulation in TE progenitors is layered over initial heterogeneous, Tead4-independent signals.
source: Thus, emerging Hippo signaling differences, starting at the early 16 cell stage, rapidly seize control of Cdx2 expression and up-regulation in TE progenitors is layered over initial heterogeneous, Tead4-independent signals.
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation data between Yap localization and Cdx2-eGFP levels.

claim: At the 16 cell stage differential Hippo signaling has been shown to be dictated by differences in cell polarity, rather then position per se.
source: At the 16 cell stage differential Hippo signaling has been shown to be dictated by differences in cell polarity, rather then position per se (Anani et al., 2014; Maître et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Most outside cells are polarized and have nuclear Yap/Tead (inactive Hippo signaling).
source: While most outside cells are polarized and have nuclear Yap/Tead (inactive Hippo signaling), a population of apolar outside cells with cytoplasmic Yap (active Hippo signaling) has been reported.
evidence: This is established knowledge about cell polarity and Hippo signaling.

claim: A population of apolar outside cells with cytoplasmic Yap (active Hippo signaling) has been reported.
source: While most outside cells are polarized and have nuclear Yap/Tead (inactive Hippo signaling), a population of apolar outside cells with cytoplasmic Yap (active Hippo signaling) has been reported.
evidence: This is established knowledge about cell populations in early embryos.

claim: Apolar outside cells have been shown to be ICM progenitors, which will eventually contribute to the inside compartment.
source: Moreover apolar outside cells have been shown to be ICM progenitors, which will eventually contribute to the inside compartment (Anani et al., 2014; Maître et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Apolar outside cells express low eGFP, similar to levels measured in inside cells.
source: To examine Cdx2-eGFP levels in different outside cell populations at the 16 cell stage we co-stained embryos with a polarity marker (Figure 1D) and found that apolar outside cells express low eGFP, similar to levels measured in inside cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Upregulation of Cdx2-eGFP is downstream of polarity-induced Hippo inactivation (nuclear Yap localization), rather than position per se at the 16 cell stage.
source: These results indicate that upregulation of Cdx2-eGFP is downstream of polarity-induced Hippo inactivation (nuclear Yap localization), rather than position per se at the 16 cell stage.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data on polarity and Cdx2-eGFP levels.

claim: Cdx2-eGFP expression level, which is a downstream readout of nuclear Yap/Tead4, rather than position is the more appropriate way to sort putative ICM and TE progenitor cells at different stages of development.
source: Overall, this suggests that Cdx2-eGFP expression level, which is a downstream readout of nuclear Yap/Tead4, rather than position is the more appropriate way to sort putative ICM and TE progenitor cells at different stages of development.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing Cdx2-eGFP correlates with Hippo signaling better than position.

claim: After quality control, 262 single-cell transcriptomes were retained from 36 embryos, with an average of 7267 expressed genes per cell.
source: After quality control, we retained 262 single-cell transcriptomes (70 early 16 cells, 43 late 16 cells, 49 early 32 cells, 39 late 32 cell and 61 64 cells) from 36 embryos, with an average of 7267 expressed genes per cell (RPKM > 1; Spearman pair-wise sample correlation ≥ 0.8).
evidence: This describes the RNA sequencing dataset generated.

claim: The primary factor segregating cells was developmental time along PC1, where a clear progression towards two different cell populations was observed.
source: The primary factor segregating cells was developmental time along PC1, where a clear progression towards two different cell populations was observed (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by PCA analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: PC2 was strongly associated with known lineage markers – such as Cdx2 mRNA.
source: PC2 was strongly associated with known lineage markers – such as Cdx2 mRNA (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by PCA analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Diversity among cells increased drastically between the late 16- and early 32 cell stages, suggesting that emergence of ICM and TE lineages at these stages.
source: We found that diversity among cells increased drastically between the late 16- and early 32 cell stages, suggesting that emergence of ICM and TE lineages at these stages.
evidence: This is inferred from the PCA analysis showing increased cell diversity.

claim: There is a significant overall correlation (Pearson correlation coefficient r = 0.6605, p<0.0001) between Cdx2 mRNA levels and Cdx2-eGFP protein levels in the same cell.
source: We found a significant overall correlation (Pearson correlation coefficient r = 0.6605, p<0.0001) between Cdx2 mRNA levels (Figure 2C) and Cdx2-eGFP protein levels (Figure 2D) in the same cell.
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis of RNA-seq and protein data.

claim: 135 ICM-specific and 207 TE-specific differentially expressed genes were found at the early 32 cell stage.
source: To obtain ICM and TE progenitor-characteristic gene expression profiles we performed single-cell differential expression (SCDE) analysis (Kharchenko et al., 2014) between the two clearly distinct cell populations at the early 32 cell stage and found 135 ICM-specific and 207 TE-specific differentially expressed genes (DEGs) (Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by SCDE analysis of RNA-seq data.

claim: At the 16 cell stage, 33 out of 113 cells clustered with the ICM and 24 out of 113 cells clustered with the TE groupings, whereas the remaining 56 out of 113 cells were positioned in a third cluster categorized as 'co-expressing' (CO).
source: Interestingly, we found a subset of the 16 cell stage cells clustered with the ICM (33 out of 113 cells) and TE (24 out of 113 cells) groupings, whereas the remaining (56 out of 113 cells) where positioned in a third cluster categorized as 'co-expressing' (CO) (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by clustering analysis shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Some cells at the 16 cell stage already initiated transcriptional linage divergence.
source: This indicates that some cells at the 16 cell stage already initiated transcriptional linage divergence.
evidence: This is inferred from the clustering analysis showing distinct populations at 16 cell stage.

claim: Both Spearman's rank correlation clustering and PCA clustering revealed that the ICM and CO populations clustered closer together and further from the TE group indicating a closer relationship between ICM and CO cells.
source: Both Spearman's rank correlation clustering (Figure 2E) and PCA clustering (Figure 2F) revealed that the ICM and CO populations clustered closer together and further from the TE group indicating a closer relationship between ICM and CO cells.
evidence: This is supported by clustering analyses shown in Figures 2E and 2F.

claim: At the 16 cell stage, 55 DEGs were found between ICM and TE profiles, with a more extensive gene network (42 genes) expressed in TE cells.
source: At the 16 cell stage we found 55 DEGs between ICM and TE profiles, with a more extensive gene network (42 genes) expressed in TE cells.
evidence: This is supported by SCDE analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Known TE markers at 16 cell stage include Cdx2, Id2, Dppa1, Ptges, Krt8 and Krt18.
source: These included known TE markers Cdx2 (Figure 2B) Id2, Dppa1, Ptges, Krt8 and Krt18 (Figure 3C) as well as genes previously not or less-associated with TE development, such as Lrp2, Dab2 (Figure 3C), Bmyc and Dusp4.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data and previous knowledge.

claim: Genes previously not or less-associated with TE development include Lrp2, Dab2, Bmyc and Dusp4.
source: These included known TE markers Cdx2 (Figure 2B) Id2, Dppa1, Ptges, Krt8 and Krt18 (Figure 3C) as well as genes previously not or less-associated with TE development, such as Lrp2, Dab2 (Figure 3C), Bmyc and Dusp4.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data showing these genes are expressed in TE.

claim: The first transcriptional differences arising among lineage progenitors are the activation of TE-specific genes.
source: Thus the first transcriptional differences arising among lineage progenitors are the activation of TE-specific genes.
evidence: This is inferred from the finding that more TE genes are differentially expressed at 16 cell stage.

claim: 162 out of 404 TE-specific genes were associated with at least one Tead4 binding site (p-value<0.038; hypergeometric test).
source: We found that 162 out of 404 TE-specific genes were associated with at least one Tead4 binding site (p-value<0.038; hypergeometric test).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Krt8, Krt18, Lrp2 and Dab2 protein expression was detected in wild-type embryos but not in Tead4 maternal/zygotic mutant embryos.
source: Additionally, we were able to detect protein expression of 4 early TE-specific genes (Krt8, Krt18, Lrp2 and Dab2) in wild-type embryos, but found no or very little protein expression in Tead4 maternal/zygotic mutant embryos (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Krt8, Krt18, Lrp2 and Dab2 are likely direct target genes of Yap/Tead4 activity in the early embryo.
source: These findings identify Krt8, Krt18, Lrp2 and Dab2 as likely direct target genes of Yap/Tead4 activity in the early embryo.
evidence: This is inferred from the Tead4 binding site association and loss of expression in Tead4 mutants.

claim: The largest change in gene expression in both lineages occurred at the 16 to early 32 cell transition, when most CO cells specified either into ICM or TE profiles.
source: We found that the largest change in gene expression in both lineages occurred at the 16 to early 32 cell transition, when most CO cells specified either into ICM or TE profiles.
evidence: This is supported by SCDE analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Within the ICM lineage, 177 DEGs were found between the 16 cell/early 32 cell stages, 112 DEGs between early 32 cell/late 32 cell stages and only 22 DEGs between the late 32 cell/64 cell stages.
source: Within the ICM lineage we found 177 DEGs between the 16 cell/early 32 cell stages, 112 DEGs between early 32 cell/late 32 cell stages and only 22 DEGs between the late 32 cell/64 cell stages.
evidence: This is supported by SCDE analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Within the TE lineage, only 21, 13, and 43 DEGs were found between 16 cell/early 32 cell, early 32 cell/late 32 cell and late 32 cell/64 cell TE, respectively.
source: In contrast, within the TE lineage a relatively mild maturation of the transcriptional profile was seen with time, suggesting a sharp specification event when CO profiles resolve into TE profiles at the 16 and early 32 cell stages. Only 21, 13, and 43 DEGs were found between 16 cell/early 32 cell, early 32 cell/late 32 cell and late 32 cell/64 cell TE, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by SCDE analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Donor cells isolated from 8 cell embryos did not express Cdx2-eGFP and contributed to ICM, TE or both lineages in chimeras.
source: Donor cells isolated from 8 cell embryos did not express Cdx2-eGFP and contributed to ICM, TE or both lineages in chimeras (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by morula aggregation assay data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Some donor cells from early 16 cell embryos started to express Cdx2-eGFP, and a small, yet significant bias was detected of Cdx2-eGFP high cells contributing to the TE and Cdx2-eGFP low cells contributing to ICM.
source: Some donor cells from early 16 cell embryos started to express Cdx2-eGFP, and a small, yet significant bias was detected of Cdx2-eGFP high cells contributing to the TE and Cdx2-eGFP low cells contributing to ICM.
evidence: This is supported by morula aggregation assay data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The bias of Cdx2-eGFP high cells contributing to TE and Cdx2-eGFP low cells contributing to ICM progressively increased with the developmental stage of the donor cell.
source: This bias progressively increased with the developmental stage of the donor cell.
evidence: This is supported by morula aggregation assay data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The ability of a single cell to give rise to both lineages sharply decreased at the 16 to 32 cell transition.
source: We also noted that the ability of a single cell to give rise to both lineages sharply decreased at the 16 to 32 cell transition.
evidence: This is supported by morula aggregation assay data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Cdx2-eGFP low cells from the early 32 cell stage exclusively contributed to the ICM.
source: Interestingly, Cdx2-eGFP low cells from the early 32 cell stage exclusively contributed to the ICM, while it took until the late-32 cell stage for Cdx2-eGFP high cells give rise to solely TE, thus revealing a different time line of fate restriction of Cdx2-eGFP low and high cells.
evidence: This is supported by morula aggregation assay data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: It took until the late-32 cell stage for Cdx2-eGFP high cells to give rise to solely TE.
source: Interestingly, Cdx2-eGFP low cells from the early 32 cell stage exclusively contributed to the ICM, while it took until the late-32 cell stage for Cdx2-eGFP high cells give rise to solely TE, thus revealing a different time line of fate restriction of Cdx2-eGFP low and high cells.
evidence: This is supported by morula aggregation assay data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Cell behavior in the morula aggregation assay reads out the gradual process of ICM and TE specification as judged by dynamic transcriptional profiles.
source: Remarkably, when ICM, TE or CO cells, annotated based on RNA sequencing profiles, were plotted in a similar manner to lineage contribution results from the morula aggregation experiments, the plots were strikingly similar (Figure 4C and D). This may suggest that cell behavior in the morula aggregation assay reads out the gradual process of ICM and TE specification as judged by dynamic transcriptional profiles.
evidence: This is inferred from the similarity between aggregation results and RNA-seq profiles.

claim: All Cdx2-eGFP low donor cells imaged (n = 5) fully internalized in chimeras between 8 to 10 hr after aggregation, with Cdx2-eGFP levels remaining low throughout and donor cells dividing only after taking up an ICM position.
source: We observed the same fate outcomes of donor cells isolated from early 32 cell stage embryos in live imaging aggregation experiments as in our end-point analysis. All Cdx2-eGFP low donor cells imaged (n = 5) (Video 1; Figure 4—figure supplement 1) fully internalized in chimeras between 8 to 10 hr after aggregation, with Cdx2-eGFP levels remaining low throughout and donor cells dividing only after taking up an ICM position.
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in Video 1 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: In majority of chimeras with Cdx2-eGFP high donor cells (n = 4/6), cells remained on the outside, maintained high Cdx2-eGFP expression and underwent division with all progeny also remaining in TE position.
source: In majority of chimeras with Cdx2-eGFP high donor cells (n = 4/6), cells remained on the outside, maintained high Cdx2-eGFP expression and underwent division with all progeny also remaining in TE position (Video 2; Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in Video 2 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: In remaining chimeras with Cdx2-eGFP high donor cells (n = 2/6), cells were internalized while in the process of downregulating Cdx2 and finally divided in an ICM position.
source: In remaining chimeras with Cdx2-eGFP high donor cells (n = 2/6), cells were internalized while in the process of downregulating Cdx2 and finally divided in an ICM position (Video 3; Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in Video 3 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Division was not a driving force of cell internalization.
source: We thus found that division was not a driving force of cell internalization and that complete downregulation of Cdx2 is not a prerequisite for internalization.
evidence: This is inferred from live imaging observations.

claim: Complete downregulation of Cdx2 is not a prerequisite for internalization.
source: We thus found that division was not a driving force of cell internalization and that complete downregulation of Cdx2 is not a prerequisite for internalization.
evidence: This is inferred from live imaging observations.

claim: Some Cdx2 positive cells can internalize even in intact embryos at the 32 cell stage, downregulate Cdx2 and integrate into the ICM.
source: This supports previous observations that some Cdx2 positive cells can internalize even in intact embryos at the 32 cell stage, downregulate Cdx2 and integrate into the ICM (McDole and Zheng, 2012; Toyooka et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies and current observations.

claim: The morula aggregation assay reads out the state of specification of the isolated blastomeres and not necessarily their full developmental potential.
source: It further suggested that the morula aggregation assay read out the state of specification of the isolated blastomeres and not necessarily their full developmental potential.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that cells behave according to their Cdx2 expression state.

claim: Embryos reconstructed solely from cells with low or high Cdx2-eGFP levels isolated from late 16 cell embryos readily formed both ICM and TE lineages by E4.5.
source: We found that embryos reconstructed solely from cells with low or high Cdx2-eGFP levels isolated from late 16 cell embryos readily formed both ICM and TE lineages by E4.5 (Figure 5B; Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by embryo reconstruction assay data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: All embryos made from Cdx2-eGFP low and most embryos from Cdx2-eGFP high early 32 cell stages still recapitulated both ICM and TE lineages.
source: Similarly all embryos made from Cdx2-eGFP low and most embryos from Cdx2-eGFP high early 32 cell stages still recapitulated both ICM and TE lineages (Figure 5C; Figure 5—figure supplement 1), although we observed a non-significant decrease in the number of ICM cells formed in embryos from Cdx2-eGFP high cells compared to embryos made from Cdx2-eGFP low or random cells (Mann-Whitney test, p-value=ns).
evidence: This is supported by embryo reconstruction assay data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Embryos made from late 32 Cdx2-eGFP low cells still mostly reconstituted both ICM and TE lineages.
source: Embryos made from late 32 Cdx2-eGFP low cells still mostly reconstituted both ICM and TE lineages, while Cdx2-eGFP high cells by this stage completely lost their ability to form ICM and only produced Cdx2 positive TE (Figure 5D; Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by embryo reconstruction assay data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Cdx2-eGFP high cells by late 32 cell stage completely lost their ability to form ICM and only produced Cdx2 positive TE.
source: Embryos made from late 32 Cdx2-eGFP low cells still mostly reconstituted both ICM and TE lineages, while Cdx2-eGFP high cells by this stage completely lost their ability to form ICM and only produced Cdx2 positive TE (Figure 5D; Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by embryo reconstruction assay data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: It was only by the 64 cell stage that the majority of Cdx2-eGFP low cells lost their ability to make TE.
source: It was only by the 64 cell stage that the majority of Cdx2-eGFP low cells lost their ability to make TE (Figure 5E; Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by embryo reconstruction assay data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Out of eight embryos made from 64 cell stage Cdx2-eGFP low cells, only three showed re-expression of Cdx2 in a few cells.
source: Out of eight embryos made from Cdx2-eGFP low cells, only three showed re-expression of Cdx2 in a few cells (4, 6 and 3 cells per embryo), two without cavitating and one with a tiny cavity.
evidence: This is supported by embryo reconstruction assay data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The reconstruction assay revealed a different timeline for fate restriction than the morula aggregation assay.
source: Interestingly, this assay revealed a different timeline for fate restriction than the morula aggregation assay.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing results of the two assays.

claim: Cdx2-eGFP high cells completely lost their ICM forming ability by the late 32 cell stage.
source: Cdx2-eGFP high cells completely lost their ICM forming ability by the late 32 cell stage, while Cdx2-eGFP low cells retained TE potential at late 32 cell stage and did not lose TE potential until the 64 cell stage.
evidence: This is supported by embryo reconstruction assay data.

claim: Cdx2-eGFP low cells retained TE potential at late 32 cell stage and did not lose TE potential until the 64 cell stage.
source: Cdx2-eGFP high cells completely lost their ICM forming ability by the late 32 cell stage, while Cdx2-eGFP low cells retained TE potential at late 32 cell stage and did not lose TE potential until the 64 cell stage.
evidence: This is supported by embryo reconstruction assay data.

claim: Treatment of embryos from the 2 cell stage on with ROCKi was shown to enhance ICM and suppress TE characteristics through activation of Hippo signaling.
source: Treatment of embryos from the 2 cell stage on with ROCKi was shown to enhance ICM and suppress TE characteristics through activation of Hippo signaling (Kono et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous study.

claim: ROCKi treatment beginning at the 16 cell stage significantly reduced the percent of Cdx2 positive cells compared to controls (35% and 64%, respectively).
source: We found that ROCKi treatment beginning at the 16 cell stage significantly reduced the percent of Cdx2 positive cells compared to controls (35% and 64%, respectively) (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by ROCKi treatment experiment data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: ROCKi treatment coincided with ectopic Hippo activation as assessed by loss of nuclear YAP and an increase in phosphorylated cytoplasmic Yap.
source: We confirmed that this coincided with ectopic Hippo activation as assessed by loss of nuclear YAP and an increase in phosphorylated cytoplasmic Yap (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: When embryos began ROCKi treatment at stages later than the 16 cell stage, there was a gradual resistance to the effect of ROCKi, with no effect of activating Hippo signaling on Cdx2 expression by the late 32 cell stage.
source: When embryos began treatment at stages later than the 16 cell stage, there was a gradual resistance to the effect of ROCKi, with no effect of activating Hippo signaling on Cdx2 expression by the late 32 cell stage.
evidence: This is supported by ROCKi treatment experiment data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Up to the early 32 cell stage, DN Lats2 expression in inner cells could induce fate change as indicated by gain of Cdx2 and loss of ICM markers in most mCherry positive inner cells.
source: Up to the early 32 cell stage, DN Lats2 expression in inner cells could induce fate change as indicated by gain of Cdx2 and loss of ICM markers in most mCherry positive inner cells.
evidence: This is supported by DN Lats2 induction experiment data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: At the late 32 cell stage, 14% of mCherry positive inner cells co-expressed Cdx2 and ICM markers, while majority (80%) of cells still fully converted to expressing only Cdx2.
source: At the late 32 cell stage we observed some mCherry positive inner cells (14%) co-expressing Cdx2 and ICM markers, while majority (80%) of cells still fully converted to expressing only Cdx2.
evidence: This is supported by DN Lats2 induction experiment data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: When DN Lats2 was induced at the 64 cell stage, most inner cells maintained ICM marker expression and did not re-express Cdx2.
source: When DN Lats2 was induced at the 64 cell stage, however, most inner cells maintained ICM marker expression and did not re-express Cdx2. Only 1% of mCherry positive inner cells switched to expressing only Cdx2 and 4% expressed markers of both lineages.
evidence: This is supported by DN Lats2 induction experiment data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: All inner cells in embryos induced at >64 cell stage showed commitment to ICM.
source: All inner cells in embryos induced at >64 cell stage showed commitment to ICM.
evidence: This is supported by DN Lats2 induction experiment data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Expression of only mCherry (without DN Lats2) did not influence cell fate at any stage.
source: Additionally, we noted that expression of only mCherry (without DN Lats2) did not influence cell fate at any stage (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by control experiment data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Loss of ICM potential of Cdx2-eGFP high cells and loss of TE potential of Cdx2-eGFP low cells corresponds to the time when cells become refractory to Hippo signaling activity or inactivity, respectively.
source: These results are in good agreement with our findings from embryo reconstruction experiments, indicating that on a mechanistic level, loss of ICM potential of Cdx2-eGFP high cells and loss of TE potential of Cdx2-eGFP low cells corresponds to the time when cells become refractory to Hippo signaling activity or inactivity, respectively.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing reconstruction and Hippo manipulation experiments.

claim: The study offers a large, comprehensive single-cell global transcriptional dataset spanning the entire window of lineage segregation with remarkable temporal resolution.
source: While existing expression profiling datasets provide only limited or partial coverage of ICM-TE lineage segregation (Deng et al., 2014; Goolam et al., 2016; Graham et al., 2014; Guo et al., 2010; Ohnishi et al., 2014; Tang et al., 2011), our study offers a large, comprehensive single-cell global transcriptional dataset spanning the entire window of lineage segregation with remarkable temporal resolution.
evidence: This is a claim about the contribution of the study compared to previous work.

claim: There is a gradual separation of ICM and TE lineages starting at the 16 cell stage.
source: We show a gradual separation of ICM and TE lineages starting at the 16 cell stage, where the first transcriptional changes to distinguish cell populations are the activation of TE-specific genes, including Cdx2.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data showing transcriptional divergence.

claim: Cdx2 is the only known downstream target of nuclear Yap/Tead4 in the embryo.
source: Cdx2 is the only known downstream target of nuclear Yap/Tead4 in the embryo (Rayon et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous study.

claim: The TE profile appeared and stabilized, while the emerging ICM profile underwent considerable maturation until the 64 cell stage.
source: Interestingly, we found that as the TE profile appeared, it also stabilized. On the other hand, the emerging ICM profile underwent considerable maturation until the 64 cell stage, at which point segregation into EPI and PE lineages is initiated (Guo et al., 2010; Kurimoto et al., 2006; Ohnishi et al., 2014); and in this study [Figure 3—figure supplement 2]).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data and citations to previous studies.

claim: In the morula aggregation assay, a single cell finds itself in a competitive host environment and thus can act according to its intrinsic lineage identity.
source: We suggest that in this assay, a single cell finds itself in a competitive host environment and thus can act according to its intrinsic lineage identity: a specified TE progenitor will remain on the outside and contribute to the TE, while a specified ICM progenitor will move in and contribute to the ICM.
evidence: This is a proposed interpretation of the morula aggregation assay results.

claim: The morula aggregation assay reports cell fate specification.
source: Thus we propose that despite the experimental manipulations involved, the morula aggregation assay reports cell fate specification.
evidence: This is a proposed interpretation based on experimental observations.

claim: When an entire embryo is reconstructed from only ICM or only TE progenitor cells, competition with the host cells is removed and some cells are inevitably forced inside and others outside.
source: In contrast, when an entire embryo is reconstructed from only ICM or only TE progenitor cells, competition with the host cells is removed and some cells are inevitably forced inside and others outside.
evidence: This is a proposed interpretation of the reconstruction assay.

claim: The reconstruction assay reveals the full potential of cells to change fate when forced into different positions.
source: As such, this assay reveals the full potential of cells to change fate when forced into different positions.
evidence: This is a proposed interpretation of the reconstruction assay results.

claim: In the intact embryo and even in the morula aggregation assay, transcriptional profiles predict TE and ICM fates.
source: Thus in the intact embryo and even in the morula aggregation assay, transcriptional profiles predict TE and ICM fates, while in the reconstruction assay and the Hippo manipulation experiments, the full potential of cells to respond to positional changes and associated signaling environments is revealed.
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of the different assay results.

claim: In the reconstruction assay and the Hippo manipulation experiments, the full potential of cells to respond to positional changes and associated signaling environments is revealed.
source: Thus in the intact embryo and even in the morula aggregation assay, transcriptional profiles predict TE and ICM fates, while in the reconstruction assay and the Hippo manipulation experiments, the full potential of cells to respond to positional changes and associated signaling environments is revealed.
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of the different assay results.

claim: By performing morula aggregation and reconstruction assays side by side, the morula aggregation assay largely tests cell fate, while the reconstruction assay reveals full developmental potential.
source: By performing these two assays side by side, we can observe that the morula aggregation assay largely tests cell fate, while the reconstruction assay reveals full developmental potential, thus reconciling differences reported among the previous studies.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the two assays.

claim: TE progenitors exhibited similar timing of fate restriction in all assays employed.
source: When comparing the dynamics of fate restriction shown by cells in the different assays (summarized in Figure 7), we observed that TE progenitors exhibited similar timing of fate restriction in all assays employed.
evidence: This is a summary of results from multiple assays shown in Figure 7.

claim: A majority of Cdx2-eGFP high cells at the early 32 cell stage produced only TE in all three assays.
source: A majority of Cdx2-eGFP high cells at the early 32 cell stage produced only TE in all three assays, which also corresponded to the time by which most co-expression profiles resolved, as shown by RNA sequencing.
evidence: This is a summary of results from multiple assays.

claim: ICM progenitors showed fate restriction earlier in the morula aggregation test (by the early 32 cell stage) than they did in the embryo reconstruction and Hippo-inactivation assays (by the 64 cell stage).
source: On the other hand, ICM progenitors showed fate restriction earlier in the morula aggregation test (by the early 32 cell stage) than they did in the embryo reconstruction and Hippo-inactivation assays (by the 64 cell stage), revealing a time window between lineage specification and commitment.
evidence: This is a summary of results from multiple assays.

claim: There is a time window between lineage specification and commitment for ICM progenitors.
source: On the other hand, ICM progenitors showed fate restriction earlier in the morula aggregation test (by the early 32 cell stage) than they did in the embryo reconstruction and Hippo-inactivation assays (by the 64 cell stage), revealing a time window between lineage specification and commitment.
evidence: This is inferred from the different timing of fate restriction in different assays.

claim: Gene expression dynamics in the ICM lineage reflected prolonged maturation.
source: Correspondingly, gene expression dynamics in the ICM lineage also reflected this prolonged maturation.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq data showing continued changes in ICM gene expression.

claim: During the 16 to 32 cell divisions a number of outside cells are internalized as a result of the cleavage plane orientation.
source: During the 16 to 32 cell divisions a number of outside cells are internalized as a result of the cleavage plane orientation (Morris et al., 2010; Yamanaka et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Daughter cells pushed inwards during mitosis often sort back to the surface.
source: However, a recent study revealed that daughter cells pushed inwards during mitosis often sort back to the surface (Watanabe et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous study.

claim: The timely commitment of majority of TE cells between the late 16 and early 32 cell stages may be the driving force of the sorting process, allowing generation of a differentiated polarized epithelial layer that would stabilize the inside compartment.
source: We propose that the timely commitment of majority of TE cells that we observe between the late 16 and early 32 cell stages may be the driving force of this sorting process, allowing generation of a differentiated polarized epithelial layer that would stabilize the inside compartment.
evidence: This is a proposed interpretation of the functional significance of TE commitment timing.

claim: Cell divisions do not cause spatial perturbation in the ICM, thus functional commitment to this lineage may not be needed at this stage.
source: Cell divisions do not cause spatial perturbation in the ICM, thus functional commitment to this lineage may not be needed at this stage.
evidence: This is a proposed explanation for delayed ICM commitment.

claim: The ICM loses the ability to become TE when the first heterogeneities in gene expression demarcating the start of the second lineage segregation arise.
source: Instead, we find that the ICM loses the ability to become TE when the first heterogeneities in gene expression demarcating the start of the second lineage segregation arise.
evidence: This is supported by the timing of ICM commitment coinciding with EPI/PE segregation.

claim: Outer cells of isolated ICMs of early blastocysts mostly formed trophoblast outgrowths, while isolated ICMs from later stage blastocysts mostly formed PE-like outgrowths.
source: This is in line with an earlier study, which showed that outer cells of isolated ICMs of early blastocysts mostly formed trophoblast outgrowths, while isolated ICMs from later stage blastocysts mostly formed PE-like outgrowths (Nichols and Gardner, 1984).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous study.

claim: There is a possible functional relationship between loss of ICM plasticity and initiation of EPI and PE differentiation programs.
source: We suggest a possible functional relationship between loss of ICM plasticity and initiation of EPI and PE differentiation programs, which requires further investigation.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal for future investigation.

claim: Asynchronous lineage commitment may be a mechanism contributing to the regulative nature of the preimplantation embryo, ensuring that the correct number of cells is allocated to inside and outside compartments.
source: In conclusion, we propose that asynchronous lineage commitment may be a mechanism contributing to the regulative nature of the preimplantation embryo, ensuring that the correct number of cells is allocated to inside and outside compartments.
evidence: This is a proposed functional interpretation of asynchronous commitment.
